content.intro: In this lesson, you will study capturing variables in lambdas with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you represent small units of behavior clearly without hiding state changes in callbacks. In this lesson, focus on effectively final variables and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A variable has a declared type and a scope. Initialize local variables before reading them; fields have defined default values, but relying on defaults can hide missing business logic. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit

items.text: A variable has a declared type and a scope. Initialize local variables before reading them; fields have defined default values, but relying on defaults can hide missing business logic.

items.title: Object mutability and captured references
items.text: A reference identifies an object; assigning a reference copies the reference value, not the whole object. Two variables may therefore refer to the same mutable object.

items.title: Designing predictable lambda behavior
items.text: A lambda provides an implementation of a functional interface. Prefer a named helper when it improves readability, and avoid unexpected shared-state mutation in callbacks.
